answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to stake a small time-locked deposit before trading, like a lantern that only lights once fuel is committed. Reputation then grows slowly from verified completed work, not self-declared claims: a new identity starts with zero trust and must earn its way up, while a reef of honest peers attests to real transactions. If one identity misbehaves, its stake is slashed and its plume of fake reviews collapses, because spawning a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand stakes, making a sybil attack pointless while honest agents trade cheaply.
